items.excerpt: Creative Bloq argues Autodesk's scattered SIGGRAPH 2026 announcements -- new AI animation, editable Gaussian Splats and rendering tools across Maya and 3ds Max -- all converge on one goal: collapsing the gap between capture and creative iteration for artists.

Maya 2026.2's new 'Bring Your Own Data' feature lets studios train their own AI models for the MotionMaker animation system using their own keyframe or mocap data, moving generative animation from a black box toward a studio-tunable, in-house workflow.

3ds Max 2026.2 makes it possible to import, edit, relight and render 3D Gaussian Splat data directly inside the software, bringing radiance-field capture into a mainstream design/render pipeline alongside its other new features.

A designer hands a full UX review over to AI and reports back: AI is a powerful partner for UX reviews but not a replacement for the expert, with accuracy coming from the domain expertise you feed it rather than the model itself.

As AI grows more capable, the on-screen UI stops being the main focus of a product -- this piece reframes the designer's job around deciding which screens are still needed at all when interactions move to agents and ambient interfaces.

An art director argues the real edge in AI generative design workflows isn't better prompts or tools but trained visual judgment -- direction, taste and critique -- the human skills that decide whether AI output is usable.
